text:
devon: Quick question about header-based routing precedence. Current behavior: x-route-signature > x-customer-id > UA heuristics > default. That means if UA matches a special mobile shard, it can override a non-signed request that still has a `x-customer-id` absent, which has caused a few surprise routings this week. Proposal: prefer explicit auth/tenant headers over UA heuristics, and make UA heuristics opt-in via a flag (`routing.allow_ua_fallback: false` by default). Thoughts?

olivia: +1 on preferring explicit headers. UX note: console needs to show when UA fallback is enabled at a route-level. We should add a compact badge on the route details: `UA fallback: on/off` with an inline tooltip explaining risk (spoofing, false positives). :information_source:

maria-plat: Security concern — UA is trivially spoofable. If we ever let it influence billing/tenant affinity or quota, we should require signed evidence or a short-lived signed header. Suggestion: signed `x-route-signature` (HMAC) + verification in gateway. Otherwise UA should be a soft hint only.

aj: Telemetry + quota angle — we should add metrics so we can see how often UA fallback actually triggers and the delta in quotas/latency. Proposed metrics: `routing.fallback.ua.count`, `routing.fallback.ua.latency_percentile` and a tag for `route_id`. That will let us roll back quickly if cost/regressions show up.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: canary change to gateway routing precedence on staging at 2024-08-18T15:00Z (code ref: ops/routing/v2). Will announce when canary starts.

kevin: For rollout plan, +1 to canary. Also recommend an opt-in console toggle per-tenant so SREs can enable UA fallback only for specific tenants (helpful for some older mobile SDKs). Default must be off.

samir: Small implementation detail — if we move UA heuristics behind a flag, we need a deterministic tie-breaker for when both `x-customer-id` and UA match different shards. My vote: always prefer `x-customer-id`, then `x-route-signature`, then explicit tenant mapping, then UA as last resort. And add an audit log entry when UA decided the route: `routing.decision: ua_fallback` with reason.

devon: Action items I hear: 1) change default precedence to prefer explicit headers over UA heuristics, 2) add per-route and per-tenant console toggle for UA fallback, 3) emit `routing.fallback.ua.*` metrics and an audit log event, 4) require or recommend signed `x-route-signature` for sensitive tenant routing, 5) canary deploy to staging then 10% rollout. I'll open a spec PR + console mockups. cc @olivia @maria-plat for UX/security review. :thumbsup:

olivia: I'll mock the badge and toggle UI. Small UX ask: when a route is overridden by UA, show a subtle warning in the trace timeline so folks can debug.

maria-plat: I'll write the security note for the PR: HMAC format, TTL, and how we validate in the gateway.

aj: I'll add the Prometheus counters + Grafana dashboard panel for the UA fallback rate.

kevin: timeline looks good. Please include migration notes for Dedicated customers (they may want different defaults).

samir: Also add a migration task to run a one-week audit with UA fallback enabled in read-only mode (log decisions but don't change routing) so we can understand blast radius.

devon: Perfect — I'll include the read-only audit mode in the PR. Thanks all.
